passage.title: Starlight in the Center Ring
passage.author: DRC BEACON Assessment Passage
passage.text:
Cold August dew soaked the grass as Clara and her cousin Leo carried the heavy wood rocker box onto the back lawn. Tonight was the peak of the Perseid meteor shower. They had waited all summer to test their grandfather's eight-inch Dobsonian scope. Clara wanted to swing the wide barrel toward the north sky right away so they would not miss a single shooting star. When she peered through the eyepiece at a bright guide star, however, she groaned. Instead of a sharp point of light, the star looked like a smeared, distorted comet with a flaring tail.

Leo clicked on his dim red flashlight so their night eyes would stay sharp in the dark yard. He reminded Clara that the bumpy ride in their parents' trunk had likely jostled the heavy glass mirror out of place. While Clara tapped her foot and glanced at the clouds near the trees, Leo stayed calm and methodical. He slipped a small sighting cap with a tiny center hole into the top tube. Before the brightest meteors streaked across the northern sky, the tilted primary mirror at the base of the tube was carefully aligned by Leo with three brass thumbscrews.

Clara watched from the top of the barrel as Leo turned each lower screw by a fraction of an inch. At first, she thought he was wasting precious viewing time on a tiny reflection that barely mattered. Then Leo invited her to look through the sighting cap herself. Inside the dark tube, Clara saw a black dot painted on the center of the bottom mirror, and it sat far outside the silver ring of the eyepiece reflection. As long as the two mirrors pointed along different paths, half the faint starlight entering the tube was obscured or scattered.

Clara saw at once that haste would ruin their view all night. She knelt on the damp grass beside the base of the scope. She offered to turn the brass adjustment knobs while Leo called out directions from the eyepiece above. Whenever Leo asked for a quarter turn to the left, Clara moved the spring screw with steady fingers. Soon the black dot glided straight into the middle of the silver ring. Working as one team, they locked the bottom bolts just as the last thin clouds drifted away.

When Clara looked into the wide eyepiece again, she let out a quiet gasp. The bright star Vega now shone like a crisp diamond against black space. Dozens of tiny neighbor stars that had been hidden minutes earlier now sparkled around it. A moment later, a luminous green meteor flashed across the glass and left a glowing trail that lingered for three full seconds. Clara smiled in the red glow of the flashlight, glad that Leo's patience had turned a blurry smudge into a clear window on the stars.

questions.prompt:
Read this sentence from Paragraph 2:

"Before the brightest meteors streaked across the northern sky, the tilted primary mirror at the base of the tube was carefully aligned by Leo with three brass thumbscrews."

Based on the structure of this sentence, who or what actually performed the action of aligning the mirror?

options.text: Leo, who used the three brass thumbscrews at the base
options.childFeedback: In Paragraph 2, the passive verb 'was carefully aligned by' points to 'Leo' as the person who adjusted the tilted primary mirror using the three brass thumbscrews.

options.text: The brightest meteors streaking across the northern sky
options.childFeedback: 'Before the brightest meteors streaked across the northern sky' only tells WHEN Leo worked—meteors in space didn't align the mirror!

options.text: The tilted primary mirror pushing against the brass thumbscrews
options.childFeedback: The tilted primary mirror is the object that got adjusted ('was carefully aligned')—it didn't align itself!

options.text: Clara's grandfather before he packed the telescope in the trunk
options.childFeedback: It was the bumpy car ride in Paragraph 2 that jostled their grandfather's telescope mirror out of place, and Leo aligned it on the back lawn.

questions.provingSentenceText: Before the brightest meteors streaked across the northern sky, the tilted primary mirror at the base of the tube was carefully aligned by Leo with three brass thumbscrews.
questions.childTip: In Paragraph 2, the passive verb 'was carefully aligned by' points to 'Leo' as the person who adjusted the tilted primary mirror using the three brass thumbscrews.
questions.parentExplanation: This passive sentence places an introductory time clause first and the receiver ('the tilted primary mirror') as the grammatical subject. The true actor performing the alignment appears after the preposition 'by': 'Leo' (Option B).
questions.retryHint: Look right after 'was carefully aligned by' in Paragraph 2 to see who actually aligned the mirror.

questions.prompt:
Read this sentence from Paragraph 2:

"While Clara tapped her foot and glanced at the clouds near the trees, Leo stayed calm and methodical."

What does the word "methodical" mean as it is used in this sentence?

options.text: Rushing through a task before dark clouds cover the stars
options.childFeedback: Rushing through a task is what impatient Clara wanted to do in Paragraph 1, which is the opposite of Leo's calm, step-by-step work in Paragraph 2!

options.text: Working in a careful, step-by-step, and orderly way
options.childFeedback: In Paragraph 2, 'methodical' means working in a careful, step-by-step, and orderly way. While Clara tapped her foot impatiently, Leo calmly placed the sighting cap and adjusted the brass screws in order.

options.text: Shining a bright white light across the damp backyard grass
options.childFeedback: Leo clicked on a dim red flashlight in Paragraph 2 to protect their night vision, not a bright white light, and 'methodical' describes his orderly way of working.

options.text: Refusing to let anyone else touch the telescope all night
options.childFeedback: Leo doesn't refuse to let Clara touch the telescope—in Paragraph 3 he invites her to look through the cap, and in Paragraph 4 they adjust the knobs together!

questions.provingSentenceText: While Clara tapped her foot and glanced at the clouds near the trees, Leo stayed calm and methodical.
questions.childTip: In Paragraph 2, 'methodical' means working in a careful, step-by-step, and orderly way. While Clara tapped her foot impatiently, Leo calmly placed the sighting cap and adjusted the brass screws in order.
questions.parentExplanation: The sentence contrasts Clara's impatience with Leo's calm approach as he inserts the sighting cap and adjusts the thumbscrews in order. Thus, 'methodical' means working in a careful, step-by-step manner (Option A).
questions.retryHint: Notice the contrast word 'While' in Paragraph 2 that compares impatient Clara with calm Leo following each step in order.

questions.prompt: How do Clara's and Leo's reactions differ when they first discover the telescope's blurry view in Paragraphs 1 and 2?

options.text: Clara wants to carry the telescope back inside, whereas Leo wants to wait until the moon rises.
options.childFeedback: Neither cousin wants to go back inside or wait for a bright moon—bright moonlight would actually make faint meteors harder to see!

options.text: Clara thinks the eyepiece glass is cracked, whereas Leo blames the wet August dew on the grass.
options.childFeedback: Neither cousin thinks the glass is cracked or blames the wet grass; in Paragraph 2, Leo explains that the bumpy ride in the trunk jostled the mirror.

options.text: Clara grows impatient about missing meteors, whereas Leo calmly diagnoses and adjusts the shifted mirror.
options.childFeedback: Paragraphs 1 and 2 contrast Clara's impatience about missing shooting stars (groaning and tapping her foot) with Leo's calm, step-by-step work to fix the mirror that shifted in the car trunk.

options.text: Clara immediately unscrews the brass bolts, whereas Leo refuses to look through the sighting cap.
options.childFeedback: This mixes up the two cousins! In Paragraph 2, Leo is the one who slips in the sighting cap and turns the brass thumbscrews while Clara watches impatiently.

questions.provingSentenceText: While Clara tapped her foot and glanced at the clouds near the trees, Leo stayed calm and methodical.
questions.childTip: Paragraphs 1 and 2 contrast Clara's impatience about missing shooting stars (groaning and tapping her foot) with Leo's calm, step-by-step work to fix the mirror that shifted in the car trunk.
questions.parentExplanation: Aligned to ELAGSE5RL3, Paragraphs 1 and 2 contrast Clara's eagerness and frustration over losing viewing time with Leo's calm, methodical diagnosis that the car ride jostled the primary mirror out of alignment (Option C).
questions.retryHint: Compare how Clara reacts (tapping her foot and worrying about wasted time) with how Leo reacts in Paragraph 2.

questions.prompt: How does Paragraph 3 contribute to the overall structure of the story?

options.text: It introduces the main conflict by explaining why the Perseid meteor shower happens every August.
options.childFeedback: Paragraph 3 never explains why the Perseid meteor shower happens in space; it focuses on what Clara sees inside the telescope tube.

options.text: It proves that Dobsonian telescopes are too fragile to ever be transported in a family car.
options.childFeedback: The story proves that a jostled mirror CAN be easily realigned in a few minutes with thumbscrews, so telescopes aren't too fragile to travel in a car!

options.text: It resolves the plot by describing the bright green trail left by the first meteor.
options.childFeedback: The glowing green meteor trail doesn't appear until the end of the story in Paragraph 5, after they finish aligning the mirror in Paragraph 4.

options.text: It marks a turning point where Clara sees the misaligned reflection herself and understands why Leo's careful work is needed.
options.childFeedback: Paragraph 3 is the turning point of the story: when Leo lets Clara look through the sighting cap and see the off-center black dot for herself, she realizes why his careful work is needed.

questions.provingSentenceText: Inside the dark tube, Clara saw a black dot painted on the center of the bottom mirror, and it sat far outside the silver ring of the eyepiece reflection.
questions.childTip: Paragraph 3 is the turning point of the story: when Leo lets Clara look through the sighting cap and see the off-center black dot for herself, she realizes why his careful work is needed.
questions.parentExplanation: In Paragraphs 1–2, Clara feels Leo is wasting time. In Paragraph 3, Leo invites her to look through the sighting cap; seeing the off-center dot firsthand shifts her perspective and prompts her to help calibrate the mirror in Paragraph 4 (Option B).
questions.retryHint: Ask yourself how looking through the sighting cap in Paragraph 3 changes Clara's attitude at the start of Paragraph 4.

questions.prompt: PART A: Why do Clara and Leo succeed in getting a crystal-clear view of the meteor shower by the end of the story?

options.text: Clara sets aside her haste to turn the base knobs while Leo guides the mirror alignment from the eyepiece.
options.childFeedback: In Paragraph 4, Clara sets aside her impatience and kneels by the base to turn the brass adjustment knobs while Leo calls out directions from the eyepiece above, letting them align the mirror as a team.

options.text: They wait for the bright moon to rise and light up the dark backyard grass.
options.childFeedback: Waiting for a bright moon wouldn't fix a tilted mirror! They get a crystal-clear view because they align the two mirrors inside the tube in Paragraph 4.

options.text: They replace the heavy primary mirror with a brand-new lens from their grandfather's garage.
options.childFeedback: Nothing is broken, so they don't replace the mirror with a new lens; they simply adjust the three brass thumbscrews to center the existing mirror.

options.text: Leo removes the sighting cap and tilts the wooden rocker box toward the southern horizon.
options.childFeedback: Paragraph 1 says they are looking at the northern sky, and just tilting the wooden box wouldn't align the inner mirrors without turning the brass adjustment knobs.

questions.provingSentenceText: She offered to turn the brass adjustment knobs while Leo called out directions from the eyepiece above.
questions.childTip: In Paragraph 4, Clara sets aside her impatience and kneels by the base to turn the brass adjustment knobs while Leo calls out directions from the eyepiece above, letting them align the mirror as a team.
questions.parentExplanation: Once Clara realizes haste will ruin their view, she kneels by the base to turn the adjustment screws while Leo checks the center ring from the eyepiece above, allowing them to align the mirror rapidly together (Option C).
questions.retryHint: Check Paragraph 4 to see how Clara and Leo divide up the job of aligning the mirror.

questions.prompt: PART B: Which quotation from the passage best supports the correct answer to Question 5?

options.text: "Cold August dew soaked the grass as Clara and her cousin Leo carried the heavy wood rocker box onto the back lawn."
options.childFeedback: This opening line from Paragraph 1 only shows the cousins carrying the telescope box onto the grass before they even look through it.

options.text: "Instead of a sharp point of light, the star looked like a smeared, distorted comet with a flaring tail."
options.childFeedback: This detail from Paragraph 1 only describes how blurry the guide star looked at first, not how the cousins worked together to fix it.

options.text: "She offered to turn the brass adjustment knobs while Leo called out directions from the eyepiece above."
options.childFeedback: This sentence from Paragraph 4 directly proves Question 5 by showing how Clara and Leo teamed up—Clara turning the bottom brass knobs while Leo guided her from the top eyepiece.

options.text: "At first, she thought he was wasting precious viewing time on a tiny reflection that barely mattered."
options.childFeedback: This line from Paragraph 3 describes Clara's impatience BEFORE she looked through the sighting cap and offered to help turn the knobs.

questions.provingSentenceText: She offered to turn the brass adjustment knobs while Leo called out directions from the eyepiece above.
questions.childTip: This sentence from Paragraph 4 directly proves Question 5 by showing how Clara and Leo teamed up—Clara turning the bottom brass knobs while Leo guided her from the top eyepiece.
questions.parentExplanation: Option D provides the exact textual evidence from Paragraph 4 showing how Clara and Leo coordinated their efforts at the base and eyepiece to align the mirror, directly supporting Part A.
